content: taskiq production pitfalls: some taskiq Redis brokers (plain pub/sub-style) provide no acknowledgement, so a worker killed mid-processing silently loses the message; taskiq-redis's RedisStreamBroker uses Redis Streams with acks for durability and is the appropriate choice when task loss is unacceptable, plain broker is not. Result backend has a race: a failed poll for a result gives no information on whether the task is still running or finished microseconds later and simply hasn't written yet - naive callers wrongly record 'failed' for tasks that actually succeeded. --max-tasks-per-child worker recycling has a known bug where the child isn't respawned after reaching the limit, silently shrinking worker capacity over time. taskiq docs themselves recommend taskiq-aio-pika or taskiq-nats as the production broker with taskiq-redis only as the result backend, not as the primary broker, for durability-sensitive workloads.
